I farm 13.1 mu under a wheat-maize rotation, and with my age, small household, and some family labor going off-farm, I will keep the whole farm in the same system instead of trying anything complicated. I have 40 years in the field, so I will stay with the practices I trust most: improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, moderate but reliable fertilizer, a few well-timed irrigations from my well, and limited pesticide use only when I expect real pressure. I will use rotary tillage because it is faster and lighter for me to manage than deep ploughing, and it fits this double-cropping system. For wheat, I will aim for a stable yield with a little more water support because winter wheat in my area depends on timely irrigation. For maize, I will push yield with hybrid seed and enough nitrogen, but I will still keep inputs controlled because I want dependable returns and manageable work, not the highest-risk approach.
